panels.title: Request rate (req/s) by handler
panels.description: How many requests/second each endpoint is serving (the 'R' in RED = throughput). Each line is one route. NORMAL: tracks your traffic; flat ~0.2/s on /metrics is just Prometheus scraping itself — ignore it. WATCH: a sudden drop to zero during a test means the app stopped accepting requests (crash or overload).

panels.title: Error rate (4xx / 5xx as % of all requests)
panels.description: Share of requests that failed (the 'E' in RED). 5xx = SERVER's fault (bug, DB down) — this is what pages you. 4xx = CLIENT's fault (asked for a missing account) — usually fine. NORMAL: both flat at 0. WATCH: any sustained 5xx line. 0.02 on this axis = 2% of requests failing.

panels.title: Latency — p50 / p95 / p99 (seconds)
panels.description: How long requests take (the 'D' in RED). Read p95/p99, NOT the average — p95=2s means 5% of users waited >2s. p50 is the typical request. Buckets now run to 60s so big slowdowns are visible (they used to clamp at 1s). NORMAL: tens of ms. WATCH: p99 climbing while p50 stays low = a slow tail (some requests queueing).

panels.title: Requests/s by status class
panels.description: Same requests as the rate panel, but split by outcome: 2xx (success), 4xx (client error), 5xx (server error). NORMAL: one green 2xx line. WATCH: a red 5xx line appearing = server-side failures; a 4xx line = clients hitting missing resources.

panels.title: Transactions created /s by type
panels.description: Successful transactions committed per second, split credit vs debit (from your bank_transactions_created_total counter). This is a DOMAIN metric no generic tool gives you. NORMAL: tracks POST /transaction traffic. WATCH: drops to 0 while requests continue = writes are failing (check the error panels).

panels.title: Money throughput (paise/s) by type
panels.description: Sum of transaction amounts flowing through per second (bank_transaction_amount_paise_total). Shows business volume in money terms, not just request counts.

panels.title: Container CPU cores (by 12-char container ID)
panels.description: CPU used per container, in cores (1.0 = one full core). Legend shows the container NAME (via Prometheus relabeling — run ops/scripts/relabel_containers.py after a rebuild to refresh names). NORMAL: near 0 when idle. WATCH: a line pinned near 1.0 under load = that container is CPU-bound. 'Is it the DB or the app that's pegged?' — this panel answers it.

panels.title: Container memory (by 12-char container ID)
panels.description: Memory used per container. Legend shows the container NAME (via Prometheus relabeling — run ops/scripts/relabel_containers.py after a rebuild to refresh names). NORMAL: app steady ~100 MiB; Prometheus itself is the big one (it holds metrics in RAM) — that's expected, not a leak. WATCH: the APP's line climbing steadily over a long run and never coming back down = a memory leak.

panels.title: Postgres active connections
panels.description: Open connections to the 'bank' database. Your app's pool allows 5 + 10 overflow = 15 max. NORMAL: a handful. WATCH: pinned at 15 while latency climbs = CONNECTION-POOL EXHAUSTION — requests are queueing for a DB connection (saturation without the DB itself being busy).

panels.title: Postgres commits / rollbacks per second
panels.description: DB write activity. Commits = successful writes (tracks your POST /transaction rate). Rollbacks = failed/aborted transactions. NORMAL: commits track traffic, rollbacks ~0. WATCH: a rollback spike = transactions failing at the DB level.

panels.title: Application errors /s by type
panels.description: Failures per second, labelled by CAUSE (from bank_errors_total): account_not_found → returned 404, database → returned 503, unexpected → 500. Tells you WHY requests failed, which the status-class panel can't. NORMAL: empty. WATCH: any line — the label names the root cause.

panels.title: Total application errors (cumulative, by type)
panels.description: Running total of each error type since the app started. A quick scoreboard: 'how many account_not_found vs database errors have I caused?' Resets when the app restarts.
